title: Querier select over out-of-order chunks is slow: a per-iteration closure recomputes the oversize-chunk size check on every sample in the hot populateChunksFromIterable loop

source.license_note: Real upstream prometheus optimization PR #18699; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up populateChunksFromIterable in tsdb/querier.go: avoid the per-sample overSizeChunk closure and only compute the chunk-size check when a new chunk is not already being cut.
task.instructions: Optimize the tsdb package for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark BenchmarkQuerierSelectWithOutOfOrder measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: populateChunksFromIterable allocates and invokes an overSizeChunk closure on every loop iteration and always recomputes len(currentChunk.Bytes()) even when a new chunk is cut for another reason.

ops_fault.description: CPU profile of out-of-order querier selects shows time concentrated in populateChunksFromIterable doing redundant per-sample size checks.
detection_keywords: closure call overhead in hot path
repair_keywords: short-circuit size check when cutNewChunk already true
call len(currentChunk.Bytes()) at most once per iteration

visible_context.issue_text: Selecting series that contain out-of-order samples is slower than expected; CPU profiles point at the chunk-population loop in the TSDB querier, which appears to do redundant size bookkeeping for every sample.
error_logs: pprof: 38.4% cum tsdb.(*populateWithDelChunkSeriesIterator).populateChunksFromIterable (querier.go); hot in len(currentChunk.Bytes()) / overSizeChunk closure
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization; profiling diagnosis injected as upstream context.
